players.product: network-on-chip (NoC) interconnect IP for AI SoCs

quarterly_data.quarter: Arteris press release: Arteris Accelerates Industry Transition to Multi-Die (09-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Arteris launched FlexGen Multi-Die, a NoC IP for non-coherent AI and HPC chiplet architectures that complements Ncore Multi-Die (cache-coherent), Magillem integration automation and Cycuity hardware security assurance. FlexGen Multi-Die supports bidirectional transactions over a single UCIe PHY, reducing PHY area, power and I/O requirements by up to 50% (company claim), with virtual-channel link technology and QoS across die-to-die links. The expanded multi-die solution is available today to early access partners and strategic customers; the company says customers are already using its technology to move from single-die to multi-die products. The release carries supporting statements from AMD (the multi-die portfolio 'supports the flexibility and productivity required for our next generation of data center, client, gaming, and embedded compute products'), Socionext (collaborating with Arteris on its UCIe-based multi-die solution, with early access), Synopsys (validated interoperability of its UCIe IP with Arteris Ncore), UniVista (UCIe interoperability with Ncore Multi-Die), Cadence (physical-AI collaboration) and Silitronics (plans to use FlexGen in an OCP-derived chiplet architecture).
quarterly_data.figure: PHY area, power and I/O reduced by up to 50%; available today to early access partners and strategic customers
